title: August and the Ghost
premise: Ulyana Okafor, a financial-crimes investigator who hasn't slept through the night since the raid that killed her partner, traces an anomalous voiceprint to a dead man's server in Lisbon — a server containing proof that a philanthropic foundation is laundering money for a planned 'accident' at the upcoming Global Finance Summit. The voiceprint belongs to August Reyes, the partner she believed died by his own hand, and the ghost's messages force her to confront what really happened the night of the incident. Hunted by the foundation's fixers and betrayed by her own agency, Ulyana follows the money across three countries to stop the attack and expose the inheritance scheme at its heart — a fortune built on her partner's erased identity. She stops the attack at the summit, but the final revelation is August himself, alive in the shadows, who must choose between the ghost he became and the justice only she can give him.
about_author: W. M. Almeida is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money through shell companies before turning to fiction. Almeida writes thrillers about people who discover that ledgers remember what witnesses forget.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She works a routine fraud case in London, flawless on paper, while insomnia and guilt over 'the incident' gnaw at her. A flagged transaction from a Lisbon shell company contains a voiceprint fragment that stops her cold: it's August Reyes, her dead partner. Beat: dread disguised as diligence.

chapters.title: The Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Ulyana runs the fragment against archived case files and confirms the match — impossible, since August died eight months ago. Her supervisor orders her to drop it. She copies the file anyway. Beat: the first deliberate step off the lawful path.

chapters.title: Dead Man's Server
chapters.summary: Following the voiceprint's routing, Ulyana unlocks an encrypted server in Lisbon containing August's hidden investigation: the Meridian Foundation, a summit sponsor, moving billions toward an operation codenamed FALLEN OAK. Beat: vertigo — the case is bigger than her career.

chapters.title: What the Incident Was
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Ulyana's POV. The raid on a data center that went wrong, the shot she heard, the report blaming August for tipping off the target. Now she sees Meridian's fingerprints on the raid's authorization. Beat: grief reorganizing into guilt.

chapters.title: Lisbon
chapters.summary: Ulyana flies to Lisbon under a conference cover. She finds the server's physical host in a decommissioned bank vault and evidence someone else has been there — recently, leaving a chalked number: 22. Beat: she is not alone in the ghost's house.

chapters.title: The Inheritance
chapters.summary: The server reveals Meridian's structure: a dynastic inheritance laundered through charitable vehicles, controlled by matriarch Helena Vasco-Brandt, whose son died in a scandal August had been tracing. FALLEN OAK is timed to the summit to erase the ledger trail. Beat: motive crystallizes.

chapters.title: A Fixer Named Sable
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Meridian's fixer is briefed on 'a London analyst' and begins closing the net — passport flags, hotel access, a staged theft. Beat: cold professional menace; the reader sees the trap before Ulyana does.

chapters.title: The Chalked Number
chapters.summary: Ulyana realizes 22 is a dead-drop protocol from her and August's old cases. At drop 22 in the Alfama she finds a note in August's handwriting: 'You were right about the raid. Trust no badge.' Beat: the ghost becomes a correspondent.

chapters.title: Burned
chapters.summary: Sable's trap springs: Ulyana is framed for the hotel theft, her credentials revoked, an Interpol notice drafted. She escapes through the tram tunnels with only the server drive and the note. Beat: no way back to the lawful life.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Ulyana, now a fugitive, weighs going public against going deeper. A former colleague, Ines Duarte, risks her career to verify one Meridian transaction — enough to confirm, not enough to prove. Beat: the cost of the truth counted in other people's safety.

chapters.title: The Vasco-Brandt Archive
chapters.summary: Ulyana infiltrates Meridian's Lisbon archive during a gala, finding the original scandal file: the son's death was murder, and the family's lawyer — now a summit security director — helped bury it. Beat: inheritance revealed as a weapon passed down.

chapters.title: Voice
chapters.summary: A dead-drop message contains a live audio channel. Ulyana speaks to August for the first time since his 'death.' He admits he faked it to survive the raid, and that the voiceprint was his beacon, meant for her alone. Beat: relief curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: What He Let Her Believe
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, furious confrontation across the channel. August explains the frame-up that targeted him and why her grief was the safest cover for both of them. She refuses forgiveness. Beat: the personal wound the thriller has been hiding.

chapters.title: Sable Closes In
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Cross-referencing the dead-drop network, Sable identifies Ines and takes her — leverage against Ulyana. Beat: the antagonist's competence raises stakes from professional to human.

chapters.title: Trade
chapters.summary: Meridian offers Ulyana immunity and Ines's release in exchange for the server drive. August warns it's a lie; she goes anyway, and Sable takes both the drive and her. Beat: the protagonist at her lowest, stripped of every asset.

chapters.title: The Ghost's Plan
chapters.summary: August reveals he anticipated the trade: the drive Ulyana surrendered is a decoy seeded with a tracking beacon. But the real FALLEN OAK timeline has moved up — the attack is tomorrow, at the summit's opening session. Beat: hope with a clock attached.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Hours
chapters.summary: Ulyana and August work the dead-drop network to reconstruct FALLEN OAK's mechanism: a staged gas-system failure in the summit hall that will kill dozens and destroy Meridian's rival claimants to the inheritance. Beat: the two partners, estranged, forced into sync.

chapters.title: Ines
chapters.summary: Ulyana trades herself to Sable for Ines's release, walking into the vault where it all began. There she finds the proof August hid: the raid order signed by the summit security director. Beat: sacrifice as strategy, fear as fuel.

chapters.title: The Summit
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV inside the summit perimeter, using her forged credentials and the security director's own signature to reach the building systems. Sable hunts her through the service corridors. Beat: rising, breathless countdown tension.

chapters.title: Fallen Oak
chapters.summary: Climax. Ulyana vents and locks down the gas system minutes before detonation; Sable corners her, but August's decoy-beacon data floods Meridian's own screens, and the director, exposed, orders Sable to stand down to save himself. Beat: the accident that never happens, witnessed by everyone.

chapters.title: Ledgers Remember
chapters.summary: Aftermath: Helena Vasco-Brandt arrested as the archive evidence goes public; Sable vanishes with a drive of his own; Ines recovers. Ulyana testifies from the shadows of the investigation she technically never joined. Beat: justice achieved, but outside every frame that promised it.

chapters.title: August and the Ghost
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. August, legally dead and permanently so, meets her once at the Alfama drop before disappearing into a new identity. She sleeps through the night for the first time since the incident. Final line: the voiceprint pings once — a new case, a new ghost. Beat: quiet resolution with an open door.
